intent: Add the lyricanki launcher icon to the shared family — a new note-ascender glyph plus its registry entry — and keep python_pkg/app_icons/_glyph_art.py under the 250-line cap while doing it, by moving two glyph constants into a companion module. The cap compliance is the last blocker to wiring the cap into pre-commit, which is why the two land together.
scope: python_pkg/app_icons/_glyph_art.py: 220 -> 238 lines (adds _NOTE_ASCENDER's artwork, loses _TRACK_BARS and _NOTE_ASCENDER to the companion module)
python_pkg/app_icons/glyphs.py: imports _NOTE_ASCENDER and _TRACK_BARS from the new module, and registers the note-ascender Glyph
python_pkg/app_icons/apps.py: new lyricanki AppIcon entry (accent #B8862E, glyph note-ascender, linux=False)
Non-goal: any change to the artwork of the twelve pre-existing glyphs, or to the shared family constants in style.py
changes: Added the note-ascender glyph and the lyricanki AppIcon entry, so lyricanki stops shipping the stock Flutter 'beach' icon. linux=False because ~/lyricanki has an android/ target and no linux/ directory — verified on disk, not assumed — so there is no desktop hicolor set to install.

Moved the two most recent glyph constants (_TRACK_BARS, _NOTE_ASCENDER) with their comments into a companion module. The division carries no meaning beyond the cap, and the module docstring says so, because a reader would otherwise look for a taxonomy that is not there.

glyphs.py imports from both modules. Nothing else changed: the Glyph dataclass, the registry and the lookup all stay put, so no caller or test needs to know which file a glyph lives in — the same contract the original _glyph_art split established.

verification.evidence: 13 glyphs load; both moved names ('note-ascender', 'track-bars') are present in the registry.

verification.command: build_svg(GLYPHS[name], '#7C9CF5', with_background=True) for the moved glyphs
verification.evidence: Ran the real renderer, not just the import: note-ascender produces 641 bytes and track-bars 444, both with the accent colour substituted. A control glyph (anvil, untouched) renders alongside them at 496 bytes.
44 passed. The coverage gate reports below 100% only because a single-package run does not exercise the rest of the repo.
'all checked files are within 250 lines'. Both modules are under: 238 and 50.

No linux/ directory (android/ is present), confirming linux=False is correct rather than an oversight. The six generated icon assets exist in ~/lyricanki/assets/icon/ and that repo's tree is clean, so the app side was committed separately as the contract's out_of_scope says.
ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, pytest-with-coverage and codespell all pass. No suppression added.

risks: A mid-edit slip removed the _NOTE_ASCENDER argument from its Glyph(...) call site as well as from the import list, which surfaced immediately as a TypeError on import. Repaired and re-verified by rendering; recorded because the import-only check would not have caught it — the registry has to be built for that failure to appear.
Two modules now hold glyph data, so someone adding a glyph must pick one. The docstring directs them to the cap rather than to a false distinction.
rollback: git revert the commit; lyricanki loses its family icon and returns to the stock Flutter icon, and the _glyph_art split is undone. Because the same commit wires the file-length gate, a revert must also drop that hook or the tree it restores will not satisfy it.
